title: Car Fleets

concept.title: A car cannot pass the car in front of it
body: Cars drive to a destination on a one-lane road. A fast car that catches a slower car in front cannot pass: it joins it and drives at the slower speed. A group of cars that arrive together is a **fleet**. The question is how many fleets arrive at the destination.

Sort the cars by position, **starting with the one closest to the destination**. For a car, the time to arrive alone is `(target - position) / speed`. A car forms a **new fleet** exactly when it needs **more time** than the fleet right in front of it (it never catches up). Otherwise it catches up and joins that fleet.

body.code:
cars.sort(reverse=True)                  # closest to the target first
fleets = 0; slowest_time = 0
for pos, speed in cars:
    time = (target - pos) / speed
    if time > slowest_time:             # it never reaches the fleet in front
        fleets += 1; slowest_time = time

body: To avoid decimals, compare two times with a **cross product**: `(t1 / s1) > (t2 / s2)` is the same as `t1 * s2 > t2 * s1` for positive speeds. The numbers can reach about 10^18, so use 64-bit integers.

statement: `n` cars drive on a one-lane road towards a destination at position `target`. Car `i` starts at position `pos[i]` (all different, all less than `target`) and drives with the constant speed `speed[i]`. A car cannot pass another one: if it catches up with a car in front of it, it slows down to its speed and they continue together as a **fleet** (it also counts as catching up if they meet exactly at the destination). Print the number of fleets that arrive at the destination.
inputFormat: Each of the next `n` lines has the position and the speed of a car.
constraints: 0 <= pos < target, all positions are different

examples.note: The cars at 10 and 8 arrive together (one fleet), the cars at 5 and 3 form a second fleet, and the car at 0 arrives alone: 3 fleets.

hints: Sort the cars by position, closest to the target first.
A car that needs more time than the fleet in front of it starts a new fleet.
Compare times as fractions with a cross product, to stay with integers.

import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n, target = map(int, input().split())
cars = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(n)]

explanation: Going from the car nearest to the destination backwards, a car starts a new fleet exactly when its arrival time is strictly larger than that of the fleet ahead. Times are compared with integer cross products.
solution.complexity: Time O(n log n), space O(1) besides sorting.

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n, target = map(int, input().split())
cars = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(n)]

cars.sort(reverse=True)
fleets = 0
slowDist, slowSpeed = 0, 1
for pos, speed in cars:
    dist = target - pos
    if dist * slowSpeed > slowDist * speed:
        fleets += 1
        slowDist, slowSpeed = dist, speed
print(fleets)
